    About

    I am a final-year undergraduate in Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Jashore University of Science and Technology (JUST), expected to graduate in March 2027 with a CGPA of 3.25 out of 4.00. My coursework spans power system analysis, power electronics, switchgear and protection, and renewable and solar energy systems.

    My research focuses on solar photovoltaic and renewable energy systems, in particular digital twins of PV plants, smart-grid technologies, and the application of machine learning to power systems. My B.Sc. thesis, supervised by Md. Tarequzzaman, develops a simulation-based digital twin of a rooftop solar power plant.

    Alongside this, I develop embedded and IoT prototypes on the ESP32 platform, including vehicle monitoring, wearable heat-stress detection and edge-based screening support, and I am exploring TinyML on ESP32. In September 2026 I completed industrial training at the BPDB Ghorashal Power Station, which gave me direct exposure to power plant operation. I serve as Chair of the IEEE Signal Processing Society JUST Student Branch Chapter.

      In plain terms

      A digital twin is a software model that mirrors a physical system and is checked against measurements from it. This thesis builds a simulation-based twin of a rooftop solar PV plant, so expected electrical behaviour can be compared with what sensors report. That supports PV fault simulation and inverter and MPPT sizing, and a bench-scale ESP32 prototype with a laboratory PV panel is used to validate the twin.
